note.text:
The gases of air are separated in industry by fractional distillation of liquid air.
1. Air is filtered to remove dust.
2. Water vapour and carbon dioxide are removed (they would freeze and block the pipes).
3. The air is compressed and cooled until it becomes liquid at about −200 °C.
4. The liquid air is warmed slowly in a fractionating column. Each gas boils off at its own boiling point: nitrogen (−196 °C) first, then argon (−186 °C), then oxygen (−183 °C).
The gas with the lowest boiling point boils off first and is collected at the top of the column.

worked_example.problem: Liquid air is warmed. Which boils off first, {a} (boiling point −{196} °C) or {b} (−{183} °C)?
steps: As the liquid warms, it reaches −{196} °C before −{183} °C.
The lower boiling point is reached first.

cards.idea: Air is cleaned, then dust, water vapour and carbon dioxide are removed before it is cooled.
example: Water and carbon dioxide would freeze and block the pipes.

cards.idea: Air is compressed and cooled until it becomes liquid, at about −{200} °C.
example: Gases turn to liquid when cold enough.

cards.idea: When liquid air warms, the gas with the lowest boiling point boils off first.
example: Nitrogen comes off first, oxygen last.

check.prompt: Liquid air is warmed slowly. Which boils off first: {X.a} ({X.ta} °C) or {X.b} ({X.tb} °C)?

misconceptions.explain: That gas has the higher boiling point, so it boils later: −{183} is warmer than −{196}.
Each gas boils at its own boiling point, so they come off one after another.

solution: The lower boiling point is reached first as the liquid warms.

pick.q: Why are water vapour and carbon dioxide removed before air is cooled?
pick.r: They would freeze and block the pipes.
w: They make the air too heavy.
e: That is not the reason in the plant.
Their mass is not the problem.
pick.y: Ice and solid carbon dioxide would block the pipes.

pick.q: What is the first step in separating air?
e: Air is already a gas; it is cooled, not boiled.

pick.q: How is air turned into a liquid?
e: Salt has nothing to do with it.

pick.q: What is the name of the method used to separate liquid air?
e: Filtration separates a solid from a liquid.
pick.y: Each gas boils off at its own boiling point.
